newsitem.title: UK: LME copper drags up from lows while zinc soars.
newsitem.headline: LME copper drags up from lows while zinc soars.

text.p: Copper prices ended more than $50 weaker but well off the day's lows on Monday after a rollercoaster session which also saw zinc shoot up to fresh 6-3/4 year highs.
Aluminium also clawed its way higher after early weakness, but the other metals were mostly sluggish and ended mixed within recent ranges.

Three months London Metal Exchange (LME) copper ended the afternoon kerb $56 weaker at $2,511 per tonne. Prices fell sharply early due to follow-through selling after tumbling on speculative liquidation late on Friday.
But copper came back strongly in the kerb and was able to pare some of its losses by the end of the day after holding at a low of $2,486.
The cash to threes backwardation continued to be a strong feature in the copper market and flared by some $10 to $137/$147, due to stubborn tightness in the nearby dates, traders said.
"The market is nervous and the spreads are tight. July/August went out another $10 today," a trader said. July/August was $89, compared to $77 previously.
"No one wants to go short of July because of the tightness in the spreads," he added.
The tumble shook out some of the weaker longs, he added, but stronger longs remain and the market will need to broadly consolidate.
Zinc benefitted from fund interest over the midday break and notched up a fresh high since October 1990 of $1,415, a trader said.
It lost a bit of ground on the kerb but still finished $9.50 stronger at $1,408.50.
Aluminium, meanwhile, was lifted from early lows to a $12 stronger $1,590 by the kerb. But traders said it might have some trouble at a band of resistance around $1600-$1605 as it tries the upside.
The other metals were generally quiet.
Lead was last indicated at $620/21, compared to $624 on Friday after leaning to recent lows below $620 in the midday session.
Tin was also dull at $560, up $30, while nickel ended $60 easier at $7,210. Alloy was just firmer at $1,467 from $1,464.
